companies.subsequent_events: 2026-08-10: closed $2.6B DDTL 5.5 delayed-draw term loan, SOFR+550bp, ~5-yr maturity vs ~3-yr avg underlying customer contracts; rated Ba2 (Moody's) / BB+ (Fitch). 2026-09-18: priced upsized $3.7B 2.875% Convertible Senior Notes due 2033 (upsized from $3.0B), settlement Sep 22, 2026. 2026-10-07: AdaniConneX India capacity partnership (240 MW, option to 480 MW). Q3'26 interest expense guided $860-940M. No new rating actions found Jul 1-Oct 9 2026 (search coverage limited). Pro forma gross debt ~ $35.6B + $3.7B converts + DDTL draws (supplemental materials reportedly showed $38.5B as-adjusted for financings at an earlier point).
companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Structure: corporate unsecured notes/converts (guaranteed by certain wholly-owned subs) structurally subordinated to SPV-level secured DDTLs backed by GPUs + assigned customer contracts (DDTL 4.0 non-recourse except carve-outs; DDTL 5.0 at CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC). Revolver $2.5B to Nov 2029 with covenant metrics modified Nov 2025 (specific ratios not retrieved). DDTL 5.0: SOFR+4.50%, 0.50% undrawn fee. S&P downgrade trigger: FFO/debt <12% with CFO/debt <10%, or tightening liquidity. Mgmt (Q1'26 call): no maturities until 2029 other than self-amortizing contract-backed debt and OEM vendor financing. Scheduled principal: ~$4.4B rest of 2026, ~$6.2B 2027 (amortizing DDTL/OEM). Customer concentration: largest customer (Microsoft) ~67% of FY25 revenue; top customer 36% and #2 26% of Q2'26 revenue (secondary, unnamed); H1'26 Customer A 40%, B 23%. Backlog $104B at Q2'26. OpenAI (~$22.4B) and Meta (~$35B) contract totals from prior extraction NOT re-verified.
companies.credit_view: CoreWeave is a highly levered, contract-backed GPU lessor: ~$30.0B net debt is ~6.8x LTM adj EBITDA ($4.4B) and EBITDA/interest is only ~2.3x, with Q3 interest guided to ~$0.9B/quarter, while FY26 capex of $35-39B keeps FCF deeply negative and dependent on continuous capital-markets access. Mitigants are a $104B+ take-or-pay backlog with investment-grade hyperscaler counterparties, falling cost of debt (~300bp lower YoY), self-amortizing contract-matched DDTLs (IG-rated DDTL 4.0) and $15.6B liquidity. The key credit risk for unsecured bondholders is structural subordination to ~$19B of secured/SPV debt plus $35B+ of uncommenced lease obligations, alongside customer concentration and refinancing of ~$10.6B of amortization in 2026-27. Ratings (B+/Ba3/BB-) hinge on execution of data-center deliveries on time and leverage trending toward ~4-5x as contracted capacity comes online.

companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Capital structure is almost entirely unsecured convertible notes (low cash coupons 0.5-3.0%, except 4.50% 2034s), no maintenance covenants identified; the Jul-2026 $775M facility introduces SPV-level secured debt that will be structurally senior to the converts. Customer prepayments (> $9B upfront funding for 2026; 50-60% of associated capex) are quasi-debt: they are performance obligations repayable/at risk if capacity is not delivered and they inflate CFO ($4.5B H1'26 CFO). NVIDIA $2B equity investment in Q1'26. FY26 guide: revenue $3.0-3.4B, ~40% adj EBITDA margin, capex $20-25B, 800MW-1GW connected power by YE26.
companies.credit_view: Nebius is the least levered of the three on a net basis (~$0.5B net debt at Jun-30, ~1.3x LTM adj EBITDA) because it has pre-funded its build with ~$8B of cash from converts, equity (incl. NVIDIA $2B) and >$9B of customer prepayments. But gross leverage is high and rising fast (~23x LTM EBITDA on $8.5B debt; ~$12B+ converts pro forma after the Aug-2026 $5B deal) against a $20-25B FY26 capex plan that will burn the cash pile, and EBITDA only turned meaningfully positive in 2026. Credit quality depends on converting the $7-9B ARR target into EBITDA and on delivery against prepaid contracts; the shift toward secured asset-level financing will subordinate convert holders. Unrated; convert investors are effectively underwriting equity-like growth risk.

companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Two-tier structure: (1) corporate low-coupon convertibles $6.75B (capped calls/prepaid forwards attached to some series; induced conversions and $1.63B cash repurchase in Dec 2025); (2) non-recourse SPV GPU financings secured on Microsoft-contract GPUs (DDTL SOFR+2.25%, USPP 5.96% fixed) and a 9% fixed facility for non-IG customers funding ~90% of capex. Microsoft prepayment ($1.9B) + IG financing fund ~96% of Microsoft GPU capex, limiting equity/convert funding need for that contract. DDTL/USPP amortization schedules and financial covenants not retrieved. 2033 Dec notes: conversion price ~$73.07, issuer call from Jun 6, 2030 subject to 130% trigger.
companies.credit_view: IREN is in transition from bitcoin mining to AI cloud: FY26 adj EBITDA was only $246M (Q4 just $19M) against $7.7B of debt, so trailing leverage (~31x gross, ~7.4x net of unrestricted cash) is not meaningful and the credit rests on forward contracted ARR ($4B for 2026 capacity, anchored by Microsoft). Liquidity is strong ($5.9B unrestricted cash plus $1.7B restricted) and ~88% of debt is low-coupon convertibles maturing 2029-2033 with no near-term walls, while the Microsoft GPUs are match-funded with non-recourse IG-style debt plus prepayment. Key risks are execution on GPU deployment/acceptance, customer concentration in Microsoft, rising secured debt (up to ~$6B more across facilities) that subordinates converts, and convert dilution/refinancing if the equity weakens. Unrated.
